precepts.text: And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. That was the promise made to us and our ancestors; that is the priesthood we were rejected from for forgetting the law.
precepts.point: Because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me. This is why other races come into our communities and run the hospitals, the stores, the clinics. Many of us do have the knowledge and ability, but they do not want us to have the capability.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me”. What does that part mean, that thou shalt be no priest to me?

There was a promise made to us and our ancestors: “And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel.” A kingdom of priests. That is what Israel was called to be.

Go back to Hosea and it tells you why we lost it: “seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God”. That is the knowledge. Usually we jump over to Malachi 2:7, but the verse tells you right there: the knowledge is the law of God, his laws, his commandments, his statutes. Because we forgot it, he rejected us from that priesthood.

That is why we are destroyed as a race, as a people, mentally and spiritually. The twelve tribes of Israel are a destroyed race. This is why other races come into our communities and run the hospitals, the stores, the clinics. The black man and the brown man do have the ability, and many of us have the knowledge to do it, but they do not want us to have the capabilities.

precepts.text: These are the journeys of Israel by their armies, and Moses wrote their goings out by the commandment of the Lord, departing from Rameses on the morrow after the Passover.
precepts.point: Moses wrote their goings out by the commandment of the Lord. The Lord gave the word, and great was the company of those that published it; so the claim that another people wrote the scriptures falls, for Moses wrote what God commanded him to write.

note.label: Exodus 19: The Covenant at Mount Sinai

precepts.why:
Numbers 33 is the record of the journeys that bring Israel to the wilderness of Sinai in the third month: “These are the journeys of the children of Israel, which went forth out of the land of Egypt with their armies under the hand of Moses and Aaron.” Israel went forth out of Egypt with their armies.

“And Moses wrote their goings out according to their journeys by the commandment of the Lord”. Moses wrote, and he wrote by the commandment of the Lord. So the claim that another people wrote the scriptures falls; Moses wrote what God commanded him to write.

The journey begins on a set day: “And they departed from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the morrow after the passover the children of Israel went out with an high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians. For the Egyptians buried all their firstborn, which the Lord had smitten among them: upon their gods also the Lord executed judgments.” From that day in the first month, the journeys run to the third month, when Israel camped before the mount.

precepts.text: They departed from Rephidim and pitched in the wilderness of Sinai, the same arrival Exodus 19 records in the third month.
precepts.point: Moses wrote their goings out by the commandment of the Lord. The Lord gave the word, and great was the company of those that published it; so the claim that another people wrote the scriptures falls, for Moses wrote what God commanded him to write.

note.label: Exodus 19: The Covenant at Mount Sinai

precepts.why:
“And they departed from Rephidim, and pitched in the wilderness of Sinai.” This is the same arrival Exodus 19 records: “they were departed from Rephidim, and were come to the desert of Sinai, and had pitched in the wilderness”.

Numbers 33 gives the journey, from Rameses on the morrow after the Passover to Rephidim to the wilderness of Sinai, and Exodus 19 gives the time: the third month after going forth out of Egypt. The two records line up.

precepts.text: The Lord is a man of war; the tribes came out as armies.
precepts.point: Moses wrote their goings out by the commandment of the Lord. The Lord gave the word, and great was the company of those that published it; so the claim that another people wrote the scriptures falls, for Moses wrote what God commanded him to write.

note.label: Exodus 19: The Covenant at Mount Sinai

precepts.why:
“The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.” That is why the children of Israel went forth out of Egypt with their armies. The tribes are armies, because the Lord who brought them out is a man of war.

Israel has always been at war, and Israel is at war today: a spiritual war.

precepts.text: Though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh; the war Israel fights today is spiritual.
precepts.point: Moses wrote their goings out by the commandment of the Lord. The Lord gave the word, and great was the company of those that published it; so the claim that another people wrote the scriptures falls, for Moses wrote what God commanded him to write.

note.label: Exodus 19: The Covenant at Mount Sinai

precepts.why:
The armies that came out of Egypt are still at war, but the war has changed: “For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh: (For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds;)”

Israel came out of Egypt as armies under the Lord, the man of war. Israel is at war today, but it is a spiritual war, fought with weapons that are not carnal but mighty through God.

precepts.text: The Lord gave the word; great was the company of those that published it. Moses published what the Lord commanded.
precepts.point: Moses wrote their goings out by the commandment of the Lord. The Lord gave the word, and great was the company of those that published it; so the claim that another people wrote the scriptures falls, for Moses wrote what God commanded him to write.

note.label: Exodus 19: The Covenant at Mount Sinai

precepts.why:
“The Lord gave the word: great was the company of those that published it.” Moses wrote the goings out of Israel by the commandment of the Lord. The Lord gave the word, and Moses published it.

So the claim that another people wrote the scriptures falls. The word came from the Lord, and Moses was of the company that published what God commanded him to write.

precepts.text: Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark when the oxen shook it, and God smote him there for his error; the Most High is serious about what is not to be touched.
precepts.point: That trumpet in the mount was not blown by Moses, for Moses was down among the people sanctifying them; the trumpet came from heaven.

note.label: Exodus 19: The Covenant at Mount Sinai

precepts.why:
At the mount the charge was “There shall not an hand touch it”, and the Most High is serious about that. Here the ark of God was set “upon a new cart”, brought “out of the house of Abinadab that was in Gibeah”, and “Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drave the new cart.” David and all the house of Israel “played before the Lord on all manner of instruments made of fir wood, even on harps, and on psalteries, and on timbrels, and on cornets, and on cymbals.”

“And when they came to Nachon’s threshingfloor, Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark of God, and took hold of it; for the oxen shook it. And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzzah; and God smote him there for his error; and there he died by the ark of God.” The oxen shook the cart and Uzzah put forth his hand and took hold of the ark, and God smote him there.

That is the same charge as the bounds round the mount: what the Most High says is not to be touched is not to be touched, and he will put a man to death for it.

precepts.text: Aaron and his sons waited on the priest's office, and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.
precepts.point: That trumpet in the mount was not blown by Moses, for Moses was down among the people sanctifying them; the trumpet came from heaven.

note.label: Exodus 19: The Covenant at Mount Sinai

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt appoint Aaron and his sons, and they shall wait on their priest’s office: and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.” This is why Uzzah died when he took hold of the ark. The ark belonged to the priests’ office, and the stranger that came nigh it was to be put to death.

Every family of the priesthood had its own responsibility in the tabernacle service, and none could transgress against another’s charge. What the world later called unions came from that order.

The bounds at the mount are the same seriousness: “whosoever toucheth the mount shall be surely put to death”, “whether it be beast or man, it shall not live”.

precepts.text: The two trumpets of silver were made for the calling of the assembly and for the journeys of the camps.
precepts.point: That trumpet in the mount was not blown by Moses, for Moses was down among the people sanctifying them; the trumpet came from heaven.

note.label: Exodus 19: The Covenant at Mount Sinai

precepts.why:
At the mount, “when the trumpet soundeth long, they shall come up to the mount.” The trumpets are what gather the people: “Make thee two trumpets of silver; of a whole piece shalt thou make them: that thou mayest use them for the calling of the assembly, and for the journeying of the camps.”

The two trumpets of silver were made for the calling of the assembly and for the journeys of the camps, and trumpets still gather the congregation at the new moons and at the start of classes.

But the trumpet in the mount was not blown by Moses. Moses was down among the people sanctifying them. That trumpet came from heaven.

precepts.text: Ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests; the priests' standard belongs to the whole nation.
precepts.point: Those breeches were made for men and not for women, as the law of the garments also shows.

note.label: Exodus 20: The Ten Commandments

precepts.why:
“And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel.”

Israel was called in this same reading to be a kingdom of priests. So do not be simple and say the law of the breeches was only for Aaron and his sons. The priests’ standard belongs to the whole nation.

precepts.text: If ye will obey my voice and keep my covenant, ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people.
precepts.point: Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: we were called by other names, African American, Dominican, Negro, but now we are coming into the understanding that we are actually the children of Israel.

note.label: Deuteronomy 26: The Firstfruits Confession and a Peculiar People

precepts.why:
The Lord avouched Israel his peculiar people “as he hath promised thee”, and here is the promise: “Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine: And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel.”

A peculiar treasure, a kingdom of priests, an holy nation: the same words Peter uses, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people. And the condition is the same in both places: obey my voice and keep my covenant, keep all his commandments. These are the words spoken unto the children of Israel.

precepts.text: Before the Most High even gave the ten commandments he made this plain: if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people, a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. Obedience is what he desired most from the beginning.
precepts.point: Sacrifice was never the most important thing to the Lord; not the blood of bulls and of goats, but mercy upon one another and the keeping of the commandments. The sacrifices were added because of transgression, the animal's blood taken in your place so the Most High would not have to kill you; you read of it from Genesis 3, where the Lord took the skins after Adam sinned. Yet there were some things you could not sacrifice for, abominations for which a man's own blood was required.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
Before the Most High even gave the ten commandments, he made this plain to “the house of Jacob”: “Ye have seen what I did unto the Egyptians, and how I bare you on eagles’ wings, and brought you unto myself. Now therefore, if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people: for all the earth is mine: And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation.”

Obedience is what he desired most from the beginning, not the blood of bulls and of goats. That is why the Lord said, “I desired mercy, and not sacrifice.”

precepts.text: Thunders, lightnings, and a thick cloud on the mount, and the trumpet exceeding loud, when the people met with God.
precepts.point: Thick clouds are a covering to him that he seeth not, and he walketh in the circuit of heaven. Eliphaz says God is surrounded by thick clouds and cannot judge through them, but that is when God is really looking, when you think he is not.

note.label: Job 22: Acquaint Now Thyself With Him

precepts.why:
“And it came to pass on the third day in the morning, that there were thunders and lightnings, and a thick cloud upon the mount, and the voice of the trumpet exceeding loud; so that all the people that was in the camp trembled.” Thunders, lightnings, and a thick cloud on the mount, and the trumpet exceeding loud, when the people met with God.

Eliphaz says “Thick clouds are a covering to him, that he seeth not”, as if God is surrounded by thick clouds and cannot judge through them. But the thick cloud on the mount was where God was, and the people trembled before it. The thick cloud is not a covering that keeps him from seeing; that is when God is really looking, when you think he is not.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 20
